text_run.content: Zilliz Cloud, as a fully managed vector database service, delivers enterprise-grade
capabilities to ensure the continuous availability of your mission-critical data and services under various failure scenarios.
Automatic failure detection and rapid failover mechanisms ensure uninterrupted service operation during node, availability zone (AZ), or region-level outages.
Comprehensive backup and restore strategies enable rapid business recovery after major incidents.
From Standard to enterprise-grade cross-region deployments, tailored to meet diverse RPO/RTO requirements across business scenarios.
Choose the most cost-effective resilience strategy based on business value and risk tolerance.
The maximum acceptable data loss, measured in time. For example, an RPO of 5 minutes means up to 5 minutes of recent data may be lost during a failure.
The maximum permissible time from failure onset to full service restoration, including failure detection, failover decision-making, and actual recovery.
Zilliz Cloud’s commitment to service availability is usually expressed as a percentage (for example, 99.95% uptime means no more than 21.6 minutes of downtime each month).
Failure of a single compute or storage node
Complete AZ outage (e.g., data center failure)
Entire region service disruption (e.g., natural disaster)
Multi-cloud deployment to mitigate risks from a single cloud vendor
Single-region, single-AZ deployment with multi-replica mechanism
Write within single AZ; WAL replicated via Quorum
Single-region deployment across 3 AZs with automatic failover
Cross-AZ writes; WAL replicated via Quorum
Active-active multi-replica architecture within region; read/write separation with fast failover
Cross-AZ writes; inter-replica sync via WAL
Multi-region/multi-cloud deployment with global load balancing
Synchronous writes across AZs; asynchronous replication to other regions/clouds
Cross-region HA will be available in November 2025. <include target="indev">Incremental backup will be available in December 2025.</include>
Same-region object storage; scheduled full backups
Backup data stored in a different region; protects against regional disasters
<include target="indev">Real-time incremental backups; fine-grained recovery points</include>
24/7 operation; even minutes of downtime cause significant loss; extremely high business value
Cross-region HA + Enterprise Multi-Replica + Continuous Data Protection
Operates during business hours; cost-sensitive; tolerates some recovery time
Non-essential systems; cost-sensitive; accepts scheduled maintenance windows
Q1: How do Standard and Enterprise plans achieve high availability?
Zilliz Cloud uses a compute-storage disaggregated architecture with three data types:
Stored in etcd (3 replicas, RAFT protocol)
Stored in object storage, inheriting cloud storage’s native HA
Managed by Kubernetes for automatic scheduling
Pods automatically respawn upon single-node or single-AZ failure
Coordinator reassigns segments to other QueryNodes
Indexes and data are reloaded from storage; recovery time < 1 minute
Avoids cost explosion from maintaining multiple in-memory replicas
Leverages log and object storage bandwidth for faster recovery
Q2: How does the multi-replica mechanism work?
Multiple StreamNodes load the same shard with primary/standby roles
Multiple QueryNodes load the same segment; data persists as a single copy
Served by any standby StreamNode or QueryNode
Proxy automatically redirects traffic to standby nodes
Multiple in-memory replicas improve read throughput
Rolling updates reduce service jitter and improve stability
Q3: How does Global Database enable cross-region high availability?
Change Data Capture (CDC) synchronizes DDL, DML, and bulk import operations
Enables cross-region/cross-cloud DR with very low RPO
Data written synchronously across multiple AZs within the same region
Write latency is at inter-AZ level
In extreme failover scenarios, data loss < 10 seconds
Zilliz health-check service detects failure and completes failover in 1–3 minutes
Primary handles reads/writes; standby is activated only during failover
Primary writes; multiple regions serve reads (nearest-region read)
Both regions accept writes; the user must avoid data conflicts
